answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits find fabricated results or coordinated duplicate claims. Auditors sample tasks and compare evidence, so creating a thousand names does not create a thousand trustworthy votes. The inlet to participation is open, but every new identity ties up capital; a lantern of public audit records helps expose repeated patterns, while a raven-style withdrawal leaves the bond at risk. The attacker pays in locked funds and audit exposure for each Sybil.
